problem: Map-based planners (A*, RRT*, DiPPer, ViT-A*) need a globally consistent map and metric goal coordinates. Odometry drift and dynamic layouts degrade the map over long-term service-robot deployment, and non-expert users cannot supply metric coordinates.
motivation: Skid-steer slip and dynamic human environments make global maps drift and become inconsistent, causing collisions or mission failure in narrow passages. Users naturally give semantic and egocentric instructions such as 'move 5 m forward, turn right, stop near the statue'. Resetting localization at each local subgoal bounds drift to the distance of a single segment.
key_idea: An LLM (Gemini Pro) turns spoken or text commands into a symbolic sequence of egocentric MOVE and visual FIND subgoals, which are executed by a detection, segmentation and motion-primitive local planner without any global map, resetting odometry at each subgoal.
insight: Combining geometric and visual subgoals is more robust than using either alone. In Table 4 the hybrid scores 88.0% on a complex mission versus 10.0% (geometric) and 25.0% (visual), and it is best in every scenario. Geometric targets work in featureless corridors while visual targets work in symmetric rooms. Constraining the LLM to a closed action set with a schema validator keeps its output deterministic. The paper reports no ablation of the LLM itself and no comparison against any learned navigation baseline.
method: Task Instruction Processing (HTN): Gemini Pro with a structured prompt, a closed action set and a schema validator outputs a JSON action plan. The hierarchy has three levels: lexical primitives (FIND, MOVE), directive resolution (egocentric vs allocentric/semantic), and grounding to coordinates.

Action Classifier: a rule-based parser splits the plan into egocentric geometric subgoals and visual perception subgoals. On failure it performs bounded exploration in a predefined obstacle-free region and then queries the user and regenerates the plan.
Egocentric subgoal estimation: the displacement (dx, dy) is rotated by the robot heading into a global waypoint G_c. Odometry is wheel encoder plus IMU only, with no loop closure.

Visual subgoal estimation: YOLOv8 detects objects and an OSNet ReID model (custom dataset) finds persons in RGB from a RealSense D455. The median depth in the bounding box is back-projected to the map frame, and a goal is set at a stopping distance d_s from the target.
Context-aware perception: ESANet RGB-D semantic segmentation finds restricted zones, cables and hazards. These are projected into virtual 0.5 m-high point clouds that are treated as soft obstacles.

Motion primitive local planner: 343 precomputed primitives are scaled by velocity and checked against an egocentric voxel grid. The selected primitive minimizes J = w_g·heading error + w_o·exp(-α·d_phy) + w_s·exp(-β·d_sem), and (v, ω) is sent to the controller.

Deployment: client-server architecture with the Husky A200 onboard (Jetson AGX Xavier) and an optional offboard RTX A4000 server. Odometry is reset after each subgoal and the maximum subgoal distance is 10 m.

numbers_note: No standard VLN or navigation benchmarks. All results come from custom Gazebo and real-world scenarios. Table 4 metric is unlabeled (assumed success %). Table 1 is a qualitative capability checklist, not numeric. Only Table 4 compares modalities and no numerical baselines were run.
results: The mapless framework reaches 95-100% success across five simulated environments and 95-98% in real-world indoor and outdoor trials. Drift error is 0.03-0.1 m, and hard collisions are near zero. The hybrid geometric+visual mode outperforms geometric-only and visual-only in all five scenarios, notably 88.0 vs 10.0 and 25.0 on complex missions. No quantitative comparison against A*, DiPPer or ViT-A* is given despite the abstract's claims.
limitations: No quantitative comparison against the named baselines or any VLN benchmark; the 'significant improvement' claim rests on a qualitative capability table.

Depends on a rule-based parser, a closed action and object set, and a maximum subgoal distance of 10 m. Geometric subgoals still drift in featureless corridors, and segmentation noise and lighting cause soft-zone grazing.

Large skid-steer platform footprint causes overlap with restricted zones in narrow passages. Success and collision metrics are not defined precisely, and the Gemini Pro LLM is a closed API with a server dependency.
